correction.text: Tondo north of the Pasig river on the shore of Manila Bay, Old Tagalog Lusong; Bulacan and Pampanga as allies only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1375, but the page's infobox gives as the state's start its 'First historical mention, in the Laguna Copperplate Inscription' ('Lord Namvaran's acquittance in 900 AD'), and the Ming trade of 1373. The page gives the area (the Pasig delta, Old Tagalog 'Lusong or Lusung') and 'north of the Pasig river', not a boundary. The shape used is the 1375 outline cut to the Manila Bay shore.

correction.text: Tondo north of the Pasig river on the shore of Manila Bay; Bulacan and Pampanga polities only allied

keyframe_review.note: 4,953 km2 (18 cells): the Manila Bay shore from Bataan across the bay to Bulacan and Pampanga. The page puts Tondo 'north of the Pasig river' bounded by 'the shore of Manila Bay', and says its influence over 'various polities in Bulacan and Pampanga' was alliance-based rather than territorial; Bataan across the bay is not mentioned. The shape is cut to a 40 km radius of Manila (7 of 18 cells, about 1,900 km2). Infobox gives no area.

correction.text: Tondo north of the Pasig river; the south bank is Maynila

keyframe_review.note: 4,840 km2 (17 cells): one cell at the Pasig mouth (Manila, Makati, Pasay, Mandaluyong, San Juan) leaves the shape and is Brunei's in Cliopatria until Maynila's row begins in 1521; the Maynila page has Manila 'probably founded as a Bornean trading colony about 1500' and Tondo and Maynila in 'territorial conflict' before 1521. Cut to a 40 km radius of Manila as for 1375 (6 of 17 cells).

correction.text: Tondo north of the Pasig river, to the Spanish conquest of 1571

keyframe_review.note: 4,840 km2 for 1564-1571, the 1497 outline; the Spanish arrive from 1570 ('Manila, Tondo, and other Luzonian towns around Manila Bay ... starting from 1570'). Cut as for 1497.

region.text: Tondo north of the Pasig river on the shore of Manila Bay (Lusong)

ledger.note: 900: Tondo appears in the record. The infobox gives the start as the 'First historical mention, in the Laguna Copperplate Inscription' ('Lord Namvaran's acquittance in 900 AD' is 'the oldest extant written document in the Philippines'); 'Lusong or Lusung' is the Old Tagalog name for the Pasig delta. A first mention, not a founding; the page gives no boundary.

region.text: the south bank at the Pasig mouth where Maynila rose

ledger.note: c. 1497: the Pasig mouth becomes Maynila's. 'Manila was probably founded as a Bornean trading colony about 1500' (Scott, on the Maynila page); the Tondo page says Brunei under Bolkiah 'decided to break Tondo's monopoly'. The year is Cliopatria's (a Brunei shape on the cell in 1497-1520, Maynila from 1521); the Maynila page says Brunei's influence 'is not considered to have extended to military or political rule'.

region.text: the Pasig river mouth between Tondo and Maynila

ledger.note: c. 1520: Tondo and Maynila fight over territory. The Tondo page infobox 'Territorial conflict with Maynila during the reign of Rajah Matanda's mother: c. 1520'; the Maynila page: 'Aganduru Moriz's account: Ache's cousin, ruler of Tondo, was taking over territory belonging to Maynila'. Where the border ran is not stated.

c. 1521: the conflict is over by the time Lakandula and Matanda rule. Maynila infobox 'Death of Rajah Salalila and territorial conflicts with Tondo: c. before 1521'; the page gives no treaty or last battle, so 1521 is a bridge.

1570: the Spanish arrive at Manila Bay. 'Manila, Tondo, and other Luzonian towns around Manila Bay and Laguna de Bay saw an influx of travelling Spanish warriors under Spanish royal command starting from 1570'; Martin de Goiti attacked Maynila in May 1570 (Maynila page).

3 June 1571: the last resistance at Bangkusay. 'June 3, 1571, marked the last resistance by locals to the occupation and colonization'; the Manila Bay towns 'started to capitulate to Spanish rule in 1571'.

region.text: Tondo, the Manila Bay shore north of the Pasig

ledger.note: 1571: Tondo passes to Spain. Manila Bay towns 'started to capitulate to Spanish rule in 1571' and Manila was declared a Spanish city on 24 June 1571 (Maynila page); the Tondo infobox ends the state in 1589 ('Discovery of the Tondo Conspiracy, dissolution of indigenous rule, and integration into the Spanish East Indies'). The dossier ends with Cliopatria in 1571.

wars.name: Brunei-Tondo rivalry over the China trade
wars.outcome: 'During the reign of Sultan Bolkiah in 1485 to 1521, the Sultanate of Brunei decided to break Tondo's monopoly': Maynila becomes a Bornean-linked rival port; no fighting or border is dated.
wars.note: Maynila page: Tondo and Maynila 'together established a duopoly on the intraarchipelagic trade of Chinese goods'.

wars.name: Tondo-Maynila territorial conflict
wars.outcome: Territorial conflict c. 1520, over before 1521; no result is dated.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Manila Bay
wars.outcome: Spanish forces under Goiti (1570) and Legazpi (1571) take Maynila and Tondo; Bangkusay on 3 June 1571 is the last resistance; Manila declared a Spanish city on 24 June 1571.
wars.note: The Tondo Conspiracy of 1587-1588 ('Revolt of the Lakans') is after the dossier's end.

certainty.note: A river-mouth port polity with allies upriver: no line is given on the page; the Manila Bay shore is natural, every inland edge is approximate.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA vs THE PAGE. (1) The row begins in 1375 and the page's first date for Tondo is 900 (Laguna Copperplate Inscription) or the Ming trade of 1373; the dossier starts at 900, a first mention rather than a founding; if a reviewer prefers 1373-1375 the 900 keyframe and event move. Whether the LCI names Tondo as a polity is the infobox's claim, not read on the inscription's own page. (2) The 4,953 km2 shape reaches Bataan, Bulacan and Pampanga; the page puts Tondo north of the Pasig on the bay shore and its Bulacan and Pampanga influence is 'alliance-based rather than territorial'. Every shape is cut to a 40 km circle of Manila (about 1,900 km2, 40% of the drawn area); the radius is a judgment, the page gives no boundary. (3) End: Cliopatria 1571; the infobox 1589 (after the Tondo Conspiracy of 1587-1588); Lakandula is listed 1521-1575. (4) Brunei: the Brunei dossier removes the Manila cells from its own shapes; here the same cell is recorded as a loss to Maynila c. 1497.

NO COUNTERPART DOSSIER YET: maynila (se-02, Cliopatria row 1521-1599 with a Ryukyu centroid, per the brief). Namayan lies beside Tondo with no overlap in Cliopatria and no event on the pages read.

PAGE BUDGET (1-2): Tondo (historical polity) and Maynila (historical polity), the second shared with the Brunei dossier. Infobox gives no area. Gazetteer: 'Manila' (place) stands for the delta; the gazetteer lacks Lusong.
